title: Follow-up: source discovery indexes untracked .claude/worktrees review checkouts
description: Found during GCLI-10 (2026-10-21), off the plan and not a GCLI-10 regression: the DEC-208 standing review worktrees under .claude/worktrees/ are untracked and not ignored, so the DEC-216 slice-1 discovery selection (git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard) lists their source copies. Evidence on this host: 'glyph callers buildIndex' in glyph-cli exits 2 reporting two matches, the second at .claude/worktrees/review-34-ccb30ef/src/indexer.ts, and '--file src/indexer.ts' cannot narrow it because that path contains the pattern. 'glyph impact ... --ref HEAD' is unaffected because a ref indexes the commit's tree. Review worktrees are local scratch and are never committed, so the proposed remedy is one line in .gitignore -- '.claude/worktrees/' -- which makes Git (and therefore discovery) exclude them; a discovery-level exclusion instead would need a design ruling, because slice 1 deliberately follows Git's own answer rather than a local directory list. Working-tree answers in this repository are the only surface affected; CI and --ref answers are already clean.
plan: Add .claude/worktrees/ to .gitignore, with a comment naming DEC-208 review worktrees as local scratch.
Add a discovery test: an untracked, ignored directory holding a duplicate source file contributes nothing, while an unignored one still does (the existing DEC-216 behavior).
Prove the evidence case: on this repository, glyph callers buildIndex resolves to the single src/indexer.ts symbol and glyph diff/callers otherwise answer as before.
bun run check, Docs and Tracker integrity green on the PR head; README or ADR text only if the behavior is stated anywhere (it is Git-ignore semantics already).
implementationNotes: Proof. Before (dev, 2026-11-17): glyph callers buildIndex exited 2 with 'matches 2 symbols', the second at .claude/worktrees/review-34-ccb30ef/src/indexer.ts. After the change, same command on this repository: exit 0, one symbol at src/indexer.ts:207:17, 5 callers in 4 files, index 20 files / 164 symbols / 522 sites. Mutation check: removing the .claude/worktrees/ line from .gitignore turns only the new discovery test red (7 others green) and restores the duplicate-index behaviour; restoring the line makes it green. CI run 44027122646 on 9791d54 green (Check, Docs, Tracker integrity); bun run check green, 84 tests.

DEC-183 reviewer verdict on opum-ai/glyph-cli#66 at head 5ef7ca4ef5752a6e56fe50bec5de76472c114068, reviewer model claude-opus-5-5 (read-only unit, no shell, ran nothing). Recorded verbatim:

VERDICT: APPROVE

opum-ai/glyph-cli#66 at 5ef7ca4 (GCLI-15). No blocking findings.

Findings
1. NIT, test/discover.test.ts:51-57: no test pins that the ignore only matches at the root. Under Git's rules, `.claude/worktrees/` contains a slash before the end, so it only matches relative to the root `.gitignore`. The trailing slash means it only matches directories. So `src/.claude/worktrees/x.ts` and `pkg/.claude/worktrees/` stay visible. That is correct today, but if someone rewrote the line as `**/.claude/worktrees/` or `worktrees/`, this test would still pass. Adding a `nested/.claude/worktrees/a.ts` that must stay listed would pin it. The `copy/src/app.ts` control shows Git still lists an untracked, unignored duplicate. It does not show where the pattern stops matching.
2. NIT, test/discover.test.ts:51: the fixture is a plain directory. A real worktree has a `.git` gitfile at its root, which Git may treat as a nested repository. The ignore excludes the path either way, so the test's conclusion holds. It just doesn't reproduce the real worktree layout. The writer's live measurement does cover the real case.
3. NIT, .quest/completed/GCLI-15.json plan[2]: the plan says "glyph diff/callers otherwise answer as before". The implementation notes only give evidence for `glyph callers buildIndex`, and nothing for `diff`. This is a record gap, not a code gap: the change is one ignore line, and the suite covers diff.

What I verified (tree read)
- `.gitignore:3-5`: there is exactly one new pattern, `.claude/worktrees/`, with a comment naming DEC-208. Under Git's semantics it matches only at the root and only directories, so it cannot hide `src/.claude/...` or any real source path. The existing `.claude/handovers/` and `.claude/settings.local.json` lines are unchanged.
- `src/discover.ts:70`: discovery is `git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard`. The PR does not touch discover.ts and adds no path list. `EXCLUDED_DIRS` (:56) applies only to the walk outside Git (:66), and it does not include `.claude`. So exclusion inside a repository is purely Git's answer.
- `test/discover.test.ts:47`: the test reads the real file via `new URL("../.gitignore", import.meta.url)`. From `test/` that resolves to the repository root `.gitignore`, the same bytes being changed, so the test cannot drift from it. `makeScratchRepo` commits it with `add -A` (test/helpers.ts:30) before the worktree copy is written. Removing the line makes Git list `.claude/worktrees/review-1/src/app.ts`, and the first `toEqual` (:54) fails. The writer's "only the new test red" claim is consistent with the code.
- The DEC-216 control is meaningful. `copy/src/app.ts` (:56-57) is a byte-identical, untracked, unignored duplicate under another path, and it is still listed. That shows exclusion depends on the ignore rule, not on duplicate content or the `src/app.ts` path. `scratch/other.ts` additionally shows untracked, unignored files still come through when the ignore is active.
- Nothing tracked lives under `.claude/worktrees/`. A glob of `.claude/**` at this head shows only `settings.json`, `skills/lore/SKILL.md`, and an already-ignored handover. A grep for "worktrees" outside `.quest/` finds only the `.gitignore` line and the test. The ignore cannot hide tracked files anyway, since Git does not apply ignore rules to tracked paths, and the existing test at :60-66 pins that.
- The GCLI-15 record matches the diff. Task moved from tasks/ to completed/ with status Done. Plan items 1 and 2 are delivered as described. The finalSummary claims (ignore line, discovery still Git-following, test reads the repository's own .gitignore, unignored control, before/after exit 2 → 0) all match the code. The discover describe block has 8 tests, consistent with "7 others green". No doc edit was owed: README:163 and ADR 0002:79 already describe discovery as Git-ignore semantics in general terms.

What a tree read could not establish
- The test results: that the suite is green with 84 tests, that removing the line turns only this test red, and the live before/after of `glyph callers buildIndex` (exit 2 with two matches → exit 0, src/indexer.ts:207:17). I had no shell, so these are the writer's measurements, unverified by me.
- CI run 44027122646 and its conclusion. Note that the record pins it to 9791d54, not the final head 5ef7ca4. The last commit is tracker-only, but the required checks must still be green on 5ef7ca4 itself before merge.
- How Git handles a real worktree's `.git` gitfile under `--others` on this host (finding 2).

Nit 3 from that verdict, acknowledged as a record gap rather than a code gap: plan item 3 said 'glyph diff/callers otherwise answer as before', and the proof above cites only glyph callers buildIndex. The diff surface is covered by the suite (the 84-test run, which includes the diff tests), and the change is a single ignore line that cannot alter a diff answer over committed history; no separate live diff measurement was taken.
finalSummary: Delivered in opum-ai/glyph-cli#66 (commit 9791d54): .gitignore now ignores .claude/worktrees/, so the Git-following source discovery no longer lists the DEC-208 review worktrees' copies; discovery still follows Git's own answer rather than a local path list, per GCLI-15's proposed remedy. The new discovery test carries this repository's own .gitignore into a scratch repo, so removing the line turns it red, and keeps an unignored copy as the DEC-216 control. Proved on this repository: glyph callers buildIndex went from exit 2 with two matches to exit 0 with the single src/indexer.ts symbol. Validated by CI run 44027122646 on 9791d54 (Check, Docs, Tracker integrity green); bun run check green, 84 tests.
